title: Type-build failures can emit source siblings and change source test resolution
content: An early tsc -b without a newly required composite reference emitted JS/declaration siblings outside GAT rootDir into dependency src directories. Vite then resolved JS and bypassed TS source aliases, causing misleading missing-built-entry errors. Record missing-reference diagnostics, remove only verified untracked generated siblings, and restage corrected project references before repeating builds. Consider preventing out-of-root emit or noEmitOnError in verification tooling.

title: Independent Agent scheduling needs an explicit root tool context
content: Actual built SDK replay exposed ambient tool-parent propagation into a separately scheduled child Agent. Host withAgentDriver validates the exact live generation, leaves the tool context only while scheduling, restores the caller context, and keeps ordinary nested parent/capability checks. Replay must assert the actual child reply reaches parent history before accepting refreshed expectations.

title: Generated references need explicit replacement ownership

title: Automated comment edits must preserve statement syntax
content: Public API annotation insertion split a return expression across a newline and changed ASI behavior. The supported compiler caught it; restore the statement, audit touched files, compare built JavaScript with comments removed, and rerun affected behavior before accepting a comments-only change. Insert by exact declaration ranges and preserve newline-sensitive return/throw grammar. The installed capture tool classifies this automation lesson as tooling_opportunity.

title: Commit checks must cover all imported foundation files and fixtures
content: Commit preparation found 81 staged-lint errors in 11 included files outside the earlier targeted source-lint reconciliation. Qualification behavior and artifacts passed, but the earlier source-lint receipt did not cover every staged foundation/test path. The final commit correction is restricted to formatting and erased completion types, with normalized JavaScript equivalence and affected tests required. Staged lint omits type analysis and reports required type-aware suppression comments as unused; preserve those comments and inspect hook changes rather than treating narrower staged checks as equivalent to typed lint.
